Quick, one- or two-page references that pair well with the workshop [modules](Materials.qmd) and the prerequisite [appendices](Resources_Folder/Reference_Material.html). Keep the relevant one open in a second tab while you work a tutorial — they're for *looking things up*, not reading cover-to-cover.

The sheets are grouped to follow the workshop's toolchain: the **R language** first, then the **single-cell frameworks** the modules use, the **plotting/data-wrangling** libraries the tutorials lean on, the **HPC / Unix** references for the Talapas track, and finally **authoring & version control**.

## R language & environment

-   [Base R Cheat Sheet](https://iqss.github.io/dss-workshops/R/Rintro/base-r-cheat-sheet.pdf) — the core language: vectors, indexing, control flow, apply.
-   [RStudio Collection of Cheat Sheets](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/) — the canonical index; everything below in the "tidyverse" family lives here too.
-   [Advanced R reference (functions, environments)](https://github.com/rstudio/cheatsheets/blob/main/advanced-r.pdf) — scoping, the apply family, and S3/S4, which Seurat and Bioconductor objects use heavily.
-   See also the workshop's [Day 0 · Module 2 — R & the Command Line](Resources_Folder/Chapter_Day0_2_R_and_CommandLine.html).

## Single-cell frameworks

-   [Seurat command list](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/essential_commands.html) — function-by-function quick reference for the workshop's primary framework (Modules 01–08).
-   [Seurat cheatsheet (object structure & accessors)](https://satijalab.org/seurat/articles/seurat5_essential_commands) — assays, layers, `Idents()`, `FetchData()`, metadata.
-   [Bioconductor `SingleCellExperiment` quick reference](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/SingleCellExperiment/inst/doc/intro.html) — the SCE container used by `muscData`, `miloR`, and the OSCA ecosystem.
-   [Signac cheat sheet (scATAC)](https://stuartlab.org/signac/articles/data_structures) — chromatin assays, fragments, and gene-activity objects (Modules 12 & 15).
-   [Scanpy / AnnData quick reference](https://scanpy.readthedocs.io/en/stable/usage-principles.html) — the Python equivalent, useful when reading cross-language tutorials.

## Plotting & data wrangling

-   [`ggplot2` Cheat Sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/data-visualization.pdf) — the grammar of graphics behind every figure in the tutorials.
-   [`dplyr` Data Transformation Cheat Sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/data-transformation.pdf) — `filter`/`mutate`/`group_by`/`summarise`, used throughout the marker and DE steps.
-   [`tidyr` Data Tidying Cheat Sheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/tidyr.pdf) — `pivot_longer`/`pivot_wider` for reshaping result tables.
-   [`patchwork` quick reference](https://patchwork.data-imaginist.com/articles/patchwork.html) — composing multi-panel figures (`p1 | p2`, `+ plot_layout()`).
-   [Color palettes — `RColorBrewer` & `viridis`](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/data-visualization.pdf) — colorblind-safe palettes for cluster and expression plots.

## HPC, SLURM & the command line (Talapas track)

-   [SLURM command & flag cheat sheet (official two-page summary)](https://slurm.schedmd.com/pdfs/summary.pdf) — `sbatch`/`srun`/`squeue`/`sacct` and the `#SBATCH` directives used in Modules 09–10.
-   [UO Talapas Quick Start Guide](https://uoracs.github.io/talapas2-knowledge-base/docs/quickstart_guide.html) — the UO-specific account, partition, and module reference.
-   [Unix / Bash command-line cheat sheet](https://github.com/RehanSaeed/Bash-Cheat-Sheet) — navigation, pipes, redirection, `grep`/`find`/`xargs`.
-   [GREP & regular-expression reference](https://github.com/niklongstone/regular-expression-cheat-sheet) — pattern syntax for filtering files and FASTQ/QC logs.
-   See also the [Day 0 · Module 2 — R & the Command Line](Resources_Folder/Chapter_Day0_2_R_and_CommandLine.html) reading, [Appendix C — grep/regex/shell](Resources_Folder/Appendix_C_GREP_Regex_Shell.html), and the [Day 0 · Module 1 — Computer System Fundamentals](Resources_Folder/Chapter_Day0_1_Computer_Systems.html) reading (HPC/Talapas + VS Code setup).

## Authoring, reproducibility & version control

-   [Quarto / Markdown Basics](https://quarto.org/docs/authoring/markdown-basics.html) — the markup the tutorials and this site are written in.
-   [RStudio Quarto Cheat Sheet (PDF)](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/quarto.pdf) — chunk options, YAML headers, output formats.
-   [Git Cheat Sheet](https://education.github.com/git-cheat-sheet-education.pdf) — clone/commit/branch/push, the daily workflow.
-   [LaTeX Math Cheat Sheet](https://wch.github.io/latexsheet/) — for equations in chapters and methods sections.
-   See also [Appendix D — Git & GitHub](Resources_Folder/Appendix_D_Git_GitHub.html) and [Appendix G — Methods-Section Template](Resources_Folder/Appendix_G_Methods_Template.html).
